editorial:
Imagine growing up in a place where the adults are all exiled criminals and the only rules that matter are the ones they made up. That is the wild world you get into here. You follow two kids, Kolyma and Gagarin, who start as best friends but slowly drift apart. One wants to follow the strict laws of the criminal brotherhood, while the other starts to question if there is a better way to live. It feels like a coming-of-age story, but with a dangerous, gritty twist because these kids are being raised to be gangsters in the middle of nowhere.

The acting is great and really makes you feel the tension between the two leads. The scenery is cold and bleak, which fits the mood perfectly. While the story moves a bit slow at times, the emotional payoff at the end makes it worth your while. If you like stories about friendship and betrayal, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a heartbreaking clash between the two friends. Kolyma has fully embraced the criminal life and its harsh laws, while Gagarin tries to escape that cycle. In the final act, the strict code of honor forces them into a violent confrontation. Kolyma ends up killing Gagarin, proving that the cycle of crime and violence only leads to loss. It shows that following these blind rules destroys everything and everyone you love.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about loyalty and betrayal.
